note.headline: Tesla jumps 5.22% to 400.0, past its valuation top; still avoid
note.happening: Tesla rose 5.22% to 400.0. That lifts it out of the 380.15–389.95 zone and into the 393.63–404.4 band, just under resistance at 408.62–420.34 (8 touches). There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Nothing new changed the business today. The move was price and sentiment only. The latest filing (2026-10-22) still shows the business weakening. Quarterly sales fell 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) slipped to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) over the last 12 months fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. The filings flag inventory up 15% while latest-quarter sales were up 0%. Unsold cars can lead to price cuts and thinner margins, so demand and margins are what is at risk. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, against 33¢ three years ago. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 37.5B, liquidity is 45.4B and total debt is only 8.0B. Share dilution is small at 0.43% a year. The business grade is D.
note.worth: At 400.0 the market values Tesla at 1581.0B. That is 15.3 times sales and 440.1 times trailing earnings. The filings note that this price needs about 51% a year growth, against 3% a year delivered over 3 years. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) built on the current 3.3B of free cash flow gives only 20.17–45.0 per share, with a base of 24.93. Even at 30% starting growth it reaches just 45.37. The other method asks what investors have paid for each dollar of Tesla's sales in the past. It gives 203.8 to 293.94 to 399.81, and today's price sits at that top. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption. The cash-flow model takes today's thin cash flow at face value. The history method assumes investors keep paying past multiples for Tesla's story. Weighing flat sales against a strong balance sheet, I put fair value in the low-to-middle part of the history range.
bull: Net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B give Tesla room to keep spending through a weak patch.
12-month sales still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B (8.3%), so the slowdown is recent, not long-running.

note.headline: NVIDIA closes 150.49 atop support as Huang-return and governance stories are reported
note.happening: NVIDIA closed at 150.49, up 0.8%. That sits just above the 147.19–150.41 support zone, the price area where buyers stepped in before. The trend is still down: the price is below its 20-day average of 169.32 and its 50-day average of 202.28, and both are falling. Today's news is commentary: CNBC and the FT reported on Jensen Huang's return and on an update to NVIDIA's code of conduct. Our data has no earnings date.
note.business: The numbers that drive the business are strong and improving. Last quarter's sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago. The operating margin, meaning the share of sales left as operating profit, rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B. NVIDIA has more cash than debt, with net cash of 23.2B. Analysts have raised next year's earnings estimate (EPS) by 27.7% over 90 days. The filings show three real risks. The margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and margins that high tend to fall back. Money customers owe but have not yet paid rose 127%, while sales rose 106%, both compared with a year earlier. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. Insiders also sold $946.6M of stock outside pre-set plans. Today's reported news on Huang's leadership and the code of conduct affects sentiment and governance only. Nothing in our data shows it changing demand, margins or cash. The shipment halt mentioned in the previous note's headline does not appear in today's news, so its effect on the business is still unknown. Demand and cash generation are not at risk based on the current numbers. The height of the margin and the quality of sales, given the slow customer payments, are at risk.
note.worth: At 150.49, the stock is valued at 18.9 times last year's earnings and 9.1 times next year's expected earnings. It trades at 12.0 times sales, below the peer median of 13.4 and in the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year range. A discounted cash flow model (DCF) values a company by projecting its future cash and converting it to today's money. Our DCF gives 194.8 in the bear case, 226.93 in the base case and 270.18 in the bull case. Valuing the stock on its own past price-to-sales levels gives 217.35 to 411.04. Every method lands above today's price. Working backward, the price implies free cash flow growth starting at 19.1%. At 20% starting growth the model gives 155.88, and at 10% it gives 105.42. Most of the gap between the methods comes from the margin. If the operating margin falls to 48%, value drops to 117.15, and at 32% it drops to 78.42. So the stock looks cheap only if most of today's peak margin lasts.
